info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package tax is how companies formed on Hanzo exchange W-9s, W-8s and 1099s with each other, from the payments that moved between them on Hanzo's rails.

get.summary: Lists the caller org's IRS return exports and where each stands, without their files.
get.description:
Lists the caller org's IRS return exports and where each stands, without their
files. Org admins only.

post.summary: Exports the caller org's return for a tax year and form, as the files the IRIS Taxpayer Portal takes, and records the export.
post.description:
Exports the caller org's return for a tax year and form, as the files the IRIS
Taxpayer Portal takes, and records the export. Org admins of the payer only: the
files carry TINs in full, so a SuperAdmin acting inside the org is refused here
exactly as at the TIN read.

It carries every furnished (or owed) form of that year and kind not already in
an earlier export that IRIS did not reject — a rejected submission filed
nothing, so its forms go out again as originals. Originals are in one set of
files and corrections of forms already exported in another, at most 250 records
a file, each written to every rule Pub 5717 §3.5 sets and checked against them
before it is answered. The files carry full TINs: the export is on the audit
trail and the files are not stored, only rebuilt from the sealed forms when read
again.

It DOES NOT FILE WITH THE IRS. Submitting through IRIS needs the payer's own
Transmitter Control Code and a person at the portal; the answer lists those
steps, and POST /v1/tax/filings/{id}/receipt records what IRIS answered.

get.summary: Reads one IRS return export WITH its files, rebuilt from the sealed forms and proven identical to what was exported.
get.description:
Reads one IRS return export WITH its files, rebuilt from the sealed forms and
proven identical to what was exported. The files carry full TINs: org admins of
the payer only — a SuperAdmin is refused — and every read is on the audit trail.

post.summary: Records what IRIS answered for an exported return — the Receipt ID on submission, then the acknowledgment.
post.description:
Records what IRIS answered for an exported return — the Receipt ID on
submission, then the acknowledgment. Org admins only.

This is the payer's report of its own act at the IRIS portal, made under its
own Transmitter Control Code; nothing here reaches IRIS, and a status is only
ever what the payer recorded. Moves: exported → submitted (with the Receipt ID
and TCC) → accepted, accepted_with_errors or rejected.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the filing, from the path.

get.summary: Lists the 1099s the caller org prepared as payer, oldest first, voided and superseded ones included — a return that was furnished stays on the record.
get.description:
Lists the 1099s the caller org prepared as payer, oldest first, voided and
superseded ones included — a return that was furnished stays on the record.
Org admins only.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year narrows the list to one tax year; absent lists every year.

post.summary: Prepares the caller org's 1099 drafts for a tax year, as the PAYER: one 1099-NEC and/or 1099-MISC per payee whose reportable payments on Hanzo's rails reach the year's threshold, from the same derivation GET /v1/tax/payments answers.
post.description:
Prepares the caller org's 1099 drafts for a tax year, as the PAYER: one
1099-NEC and/or 1099-MISC per payee whose reportable payments on Hanzo's rails
reach the year's threshold, from the same derivation GET /v1/tax/payments
answers. Org admins only.

Each draft carries the payee as its W-9 names it — under a live grant, and
otherwise only its org id — its boxes, box 4, the due dates, the payments it
sums, and backup withholding at 24% when the payer holds no TIN for the payee
(IRC §3406(a)(1)(A)) — an uncertified W-9 is stated as a warning, not a
withholding, because these payments do not require the certification. Preparing
again refreshes a draft or reviewed form in place (a reviewed one goes back to
draft, to be reviewed again); one payee has at most one live form per kind and
year, so a second preparation racing the first is refused, never doubled. A form
already furnished is left alone and named in skipped — change it by correcting
it. Nothing is furnished to anyone and nothing is filed with the IRS.

get.summary: Reads one 1099 the caller org prepared as payer, every box and both parties, TINs masked.
get.description:
Reads one 1099 the caller org prepared as payer, every box and both parties,
TINs masked. Org admins only; another org's form is not found.

post.summary: Corrects a furnished (or owed) 1099 with a NEW form that supersedes it.
post.description:
Corrects a furnished (or owed) 1099 with a NEW form that supersedes it. Org
admins only.

The furnished form is never changed: the correction is a second form, marked
CORRECTED, carrying the original's account number and naming the form it
supersedes, and it goes through review and furnishing like any other. State the
corrected boxes, or omit them to derive the year again from the payments and the
payee's current W-9. A form already superseded is corrected by correcting its
successor. It files nothing with the IRS.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the furnished form to correct, from the path.

post.summary: Furnishes Copy B of a reviewed 1099 to its payee.
post.description:
Furnishes Copy B of a reviewed 1099 to its payee. Org admins only.

When the payee's tax profile consents to electronic delivery, Copy B is
delivered into the payee's /v1/tax/inbox and the form is furnished. Otherwise it
is OWED on paper at the payee's address: mailing it is the payer's, and
POST /v1/tax/forms/{id}/mailed records it. Either way the statement is final
from this call — the form can no longer change, only be corrected. Calling it
again on a form furnished electronically re-delivers Copy B if the inbox lacks
it, and changes nothing else.

It does not file anything with the IRS, and it does not send the notice of
posting Pub 1099 Part M asks a furnisher to give an electronic recipient; the
statement is in the recipient's inbox, and telling them so is the payer's.

post.summary: Records that the payer mailed a paper Copy B it owed.
post.description:
Records that the payer mailed a paper Copy B it owed. Org admins only.

Mailing is the payer's act, done outside Hanzo; this is the record of it, made
by the person who did it and kept on the audit trail. Nothing here mails
anything.

get.summary: Download a 1099 the org prepared, as a PDF
get.description:
Answers one 1099 the caller org prepared as payer as a one-page PDF — `application/pdf` under a Content-Disposition naming the form — rendered from the form's own content: the payer's copy by default, or Copy B (For Recipient) with `?copy=B` for a statement owed on paper. The recipient's TIN is truncated; the payer's prints in full, as the law requires on every form.

The render is a pure function of the form, so the same form renders the same bytes every time. Org admins only; another org's form is not found. It files nothing and mails nothing.

post.summary: Marks a draft 1099 reviewed — a person has checked it.
post.description:
Marks a draft 1099 reviewed — a person has checked it. Only a reviewed form can
be furnished. Org admins only.

post.summary: Voids a draft or reviewed 1099, which is then never furnished or filed.
post.description:
Voids a draft or reviewed 1099, which is then never furnished or filed. A form
already furnished cannot be voided: it is corrected, and a correction to zero
is how a furnished return is withdrawn (Pub 1099 Part H). Org admins only.

get.summary: Lists the Copy B statements furnished to the caller org — every 1099 a payer on Hanzo delivered to it electronically, corrected ones beside the ones they supersede.
get.description:
Lists the Copy B statements furnished to the caller org — every 1099 a payer on
Hanzo delivered to it electronically, corrected ones beside the ones they
supersede. Any member may read it; nothing here can be changed or removed.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year narrows the list to one tax year; absent lists every year.

get.summary: Reads one Copy B furnished to the caller org.
get.description:
Reads one Copy B furnished to the caller org. Any member may read it; another
org's statement is not found.

get.summary: Download a Copy B furnished to the org, as a PDF
get.description:
Answers one Copy B furnished to the caller org as a one-page PDF — `application/pdf` under a Content-Disposition naming the form — rendered from the statement exactly as it was furnished, which can never change. The recipient's own TIN is truncated; the payer's prints in full.

Any member of the recipient org may download it; another org's statement is not found.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's tax year as a PAYER: every payment it made to another org in that calendar year, on any rail, as the event plane records it, each classified — reportable or not, in which 1099 box, and the rule that decided it, with its source — and each payee's totals tested against the year's threshold.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's tax year as a PAYER: every payment it made to another
org in that calendar year, on any rail, as the event plane records it, each
classified — reportable or not, in which 1099 box, and the rule that decided it,
with its source — and each payee's totals tested against the year's threshold.

The rules applied: a payment settled by a card or a third-party settlement
network is reported on Form 1099-K by the settlement entity, not here; a payment
for merchandise is not reported; a payment to a corporation is generally not
reported, except for legal services; a payment in a digital asset is reported at
its fair market value on the date paid; a box is reported only at or above the
year's threshold — $600 through 2025, $2,000 for 2026 under P.L. 119-21, and not
guessed for a year the IRS has not yet published. A payee's classification comes
only from a W-9 it granted the caller; without one, nothing establishes an
exemption.

Org admins only. It reads; it prepares nothing and files nothing.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year is the calendar year the payments were made in, e.g. 2026.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's own tax profile — every line of its Form W-9, W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E, every number masked to its last four characters, where the certification stands, whether a W-8 is valid and when it expires, and whether the org consents to receive its 1099s electronically.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's own tax profile — every line of its Form W-9, W-8BEN or
W-8BEN-E, every number masked to its last four characters, where the
certification stands, whether a W-8 is valid and when it expires, and whether
the org consents to receive its 1099s electronically.

Any member may read it. 404 until an admin writes one. No full number is ever in
this answer.

put.summary: Writes the caller org's tax profile — its Form W-9, or its Form W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E when it is a foreign person — and answers it, every number masked.
put.description:
Writes the caller org's tax profile — its Form W-9, or its Form W-8BEN or
W-8BEN-E when it is a foreign person — and answers it, every number masked. Org
admins only.

A U.S. TIN is validated before it is kept — nine digits; an EIN's prefix must be
one the IRS assigns; an SSN never begins 000, 666 or 9xx and has no zero group
or serial; an ITIN's middle digits are in the IRS ranges. A foreign TIN is the
issuing jurisdiction's and is checked only for its characters. Every number is
sealed under this org's own data key before it is written. Validating the
FORMAT is all this does: whether the IRS has the number on file under this name
is IRS TIN Matching, which a payer runs through IRS e-Services.

A W-8 is refused where the form itself says it is the wrong one: a U.S. citizen,
a U.S. permanent residence or an entity organized in the United States is a U.S.
person and files a W-9. A treaty claim needs a U.S. or foreign TIN on the form
(Instructions for Form W-8BEN, line 5; for Form W-8BEN-E, line 8), and names the
country of the permanent residence address.

Changing any fact on the form makes a new version, and the certification no
longer covers it: certify again. For a W-8 that is the "change in circumstances"
the instructions end its validity on. Changing only the consent does not.

post.summary: Signs the caller org's certification — Form W-9 Part II, Form W-8BEN Part III or Form W-8BEN-E Part XXX — through /v1/legal's e-signature.
post.description:
Signs the caller org's certification — Form W-9 Part II, Form W-8BEN Part III or
Form W-8BEN-E Part XXX — through /v1/legal's e-signature. The org's own admins
only, and the admin is the signer: a SuperAdmin acting inside the org is not a
person who can certify for it.

The first call renders the certification — the IRS's own certification text over
this profile's facts, every number truncated — as a /v1/legal document and opens
its signature request with the calling admin as signer; the answer is `pending` with
the document id. The signer completes it where every /v1/legal signature is
completed (POST /v1/legal/documents/{id}/sign/complete). Calling this again then
asks legal whether the document is signed and by whom: signed by the signer, the
profile is recorded certified; not yet signed, it answers `pending` again; signed
by anyone else — another member, a key — or voided, it is not the signer's
certification, and a fresh request is opened in its place.

A certification covers one profile version: writing any fact on the form
afterwards voids it. A certified W-8 is valid through the last day of the third
calendar year after the year it was signed (Instructions for Form W-8BEN and
W-8BEN-E, Rev. 10-2021); certifying it again after that renews it. It is not a
statement that a TIN matches IRS records — that is IRS TIN Matching, which only
a payer enrolled in IRS e-Services can run.

get.summary: Lists the caller org's W-9 relationships on both sides: the W-9s it asked its payees for, with where each stands, and the requests other orgs made for its own W-9.
get.description:
Lists the caller org's W-9 relationships on both sides: the W-9s it asked its
payees for, with where each stands, and the requests other orgs made for its
own W-9. Org admins only. No W-9 content is in the list; read one to see it.

post.summary: Asks another org for its W-9, as the org that pays it.
post.description:
Asks another org for its W-9, as the org that pays it. Org admins only.

A request is refused unless the caller has paid that org on Hanzo's rails, or
has asked /v1/principal whether it may — a W-9 is asked for by a payer, of a payee,
and the payments, or a payment the caller is about to make, are what say which
companies those are. The form is needed BEFORE the first payment: withholding
is decided when a payment is made, not when it is reported. The request lands with the payee, whose admin grants or
declines it; until it is granted the caller sees its status and nothing of the
payee's W-9. Asking again updates the category, and re-opens a request the
payee declined or revoked.

Category is the caller's statement of what it pays this payee for, and decides
the 1099 box: services and attorney go to 1099-NEC box 1a, rents, royalties
and other to 1099-MISC boxes 1, 2 and 3; merchandise is not reported.

get.summary: Reads one W-9 relationship from the caller's side.
get.description:
Reads one W-9 relationship from the caller's side. Org admins only.

As the PAYER, the answer carries the payee's W-9 — every line, the TIN masked
to its last four digits, and whether it is certified — but only while the
payee's grant is live; before it is granted, and after it is declined or
revoked, there is no W-9 in the answer. As the PAYEE, it is the request and
where it stands.

post.summary: Declines a request for this org's W-9.
post.description:
Declines a request for this org's W-9. The payer keeps seeing only the status.
Org admins of the payee only.

post.summary: Grants the payer that asked a live read of this org's W-9 — every line, the TIN masked, and the full TIN to that payer's org admins alone, each read audited.
post.description:
Grants the payer that asked a live read of this org's W-9 — every line, the TIN
masked, and the full TIN to that payer's org admins alone, each read audited.
Org admins of the payee only. Needs a tax profile to grant.

post.summary: Records the result of IRS TIN Matching for a payee, as the payer.
post.description:
Records the result of IRS TIN Matching for a payee, as the payer. Org admins of
the payer only, on a live grant.

It does not run TIN Matching. That is an IRS e-Services program a payer enrolls
in and runs itself, on the name and TIN it holds; this records what the IRS
answered so it sits beside the W-9 and on the audit trail. Nothing here ever
records a match the payer did not report.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the relationship, from the path.

post.summary: Revokes a W-9 this org granted.
post.description:
Revokes a W-9 this org granted. From the moment it is revoked the payer reads
nothing of the W-9 and no full TIN. A 1099 the payer already prepared keeps the
TIN it was prepared with — the payer must keep it to file — and that TIN is
never answered in full outside the payer's IRS filing export. Org admins of the
payee only.

get.summary: Reads a payee's TIN in full — and, for a payee on a W-8, its foreign TIN, which the payer's Form 1042-S carries.
get.description:
Reads a payee's TIN in full — and, for a payee on a W-8, its foreign TIN, which
the payer's Form 1042-S carries. Only an org admin of the PAYER, only while the
payee's grant is live, and every read is on the audit trail before a number is
answered — a read the trail cannot record is refused.

This is the one place a TIN leaves the platform in full, apart from the IRS
filing export. SuperAdmin is not admitted: platform authority is not a reason
to read a company's TIN.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

city.description: City is the city or town.

country.description: Country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; "US" when absent.

line1.description:
Line1 is the number, street, and apartment or suite. No periods or "#":
IRIS rejects them in an address line.

line2.description: Line2 continues the street address, when there is more of it.

state.description: State is the two-letter state or territory code.

zip.description: ZIP is five or nine digits.

box.description: Box is the box number, e.g. "1a".

cents.description: Cents is the amount in cents.

label.description: Label is the box's caption on the form.

by.description: By is who signed it: the IAM user legal recorded completing the signature.

document.description: Document is the /v1/legal document that carries the signature.

signed.description: Signed is when legal reported the document signed, unix seconds.

signer.description:
Signer is the IAM user the signature was opened for — the admin who asked.
Only that user's completion certifies: a completion anyone else recorded is
not their signature, and a fresh request is opened in its place.

status.description: Status is none, pending (a signature is open) or certified.

version.description:
Version is the profile version the signature covers. Changing any W-9 fact
makes a new version, and the certification no longer covers it.

at.description: At is when the consent was given or withdrawn, unix seconds.

by.description: By is the IAM user who gave or withdrew it.

electronic.description:
Electronic is true while the consent stands. Withdrawing it sends every
statement furnished afterwards on paper.

file.description: File is the date the return is due to the IRS, electronically (IRIS).

furnish.description: Furnish is the date Copy B is due to the recipient.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when it was exported, unix seconds.

due.description: Due is when the return is due to the IRS.

forms.description: Forms are the form ids the filing carries.

kind.description: Kind is 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC — one per filing, as IRIS takes them.

layout.description: Layout says what the files are.

missingTin.description: MissingTIN are forms filed with no recipient TIN.

receiptId.description: ReceiptID is the Receipt ID IRIS returned, once the payer recorded one.

status.description:
Status is exported, submitted, accepted, accepted_with_errors or rejected.
Only the payer's own record moves it past exported: nothing here submits.

steps.description: Steps are what remains for the payer to do, in order.

tcc.description: TCC is the payer's IRIS Transmitter Control Code, once it recorded a submission.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when its status last moved, unix seconds.

account.description:
Account is the account number the form prints — the original form's id,
which a correction keeps, so the IRS can tie the two.

backup.description: Backup is the backup withholding the form carries.

boxes.description: Boxes are the figures, box 4 (federal income tax withheld) included.

certified.description: Certified is whether the payee's W-9 was certified when the form was prepared.

corrected.description: Corrected is true for a form that corrects one already furnished.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the form was prepared, unix seconds.

delivery.description: Delivery is electronic (Copy B in the payee's inbox) or paper, once furnished.

due.description: Due is when Copy B is due to the payee and the return to the IRS.

furnishedAt.description: FurnishedAt is when Copy B was delivered in the inbox, or marked owed on paper.

mailedAt.description: MailedAt is when the payer recorded mailing a paper Copy B.

notes.description: Notes are what still needs a person, in words.

payments.description: Payments are the rail payment ids summed into the boxes.

reason.description: Reason is why a corrected form was made.

status.description: Status is draft, reviewed, furnished, owed or void.

supersededBy.description: SupersededBy is the form that corrects this one, once there is one.

supersedes.description: Supersedes is the form this one corrects.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when its status last moved, unix seconds.

w9.description: W9 is where the payer's W-9 request stood when the form was prepared.

year.description: Year is the calendar year the payments were made.

payees.description: Payees is every org the caller paid, by org id.

source.description: Source names where the year's numbers were read.

thresholdCents.description: ThresholdCents is the §6041(a) threshold for the year.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is its fair market value in U.S. dollars on the date paid, in
cents — for a U.S. dollar payment, what was paid.

id.description: ID is the economic event's id.

memo.description: Memo is what was bought, in the rail's words.

proof.description: Proof is the rail's own reference for the payment.

rail.description: Rail is how it moved: x402, ledger, chain, ach, wire, card, network or other.

verdict.description: Verdict is whether it is reportable, where, and the rules that decided it.

at.description: At is when the payer recorded it, unix seconds.

by.description: By is the admin who recorded it.

result.description: Result is what IRS TIN Matching answered: matched or mismatched.

csv.description:
CSV is the file itself. It carries full TINs, and is answered only to an org
admin of the payer, on the audit trail.

digest.description: Digest is the SHA-256 of its bytes, hex, so a re-read proves it is the same file.

name.description: Name is the file name, e.g. "1099-NEC-2026-original-1.csv".

records.description: Records is how many forms it holds, at most 250.

type.description: Type is original or correction: the portal takes them apart.

address.description: Address is where the form says they are.

businessName.description: BusinessName is W-9 line 2, when there is one.

phone.description: Phone is the payer's telephone number; a recipient has none on the form.

tin.description:
TIN is masked here always. The recipient's is truncated on Copy B as Pub 1099
allows; the payer's prints in full on the form itself, where the law requires it.

tinType.description: TINType is ssn or ein; empty when no TIN is held.

category.description:
Category is what the payer states it bought from this payee; services when
it has stated nothing.

lines.description: Lines are the payments, oldest first.

totals.description: Totals are the reportable sums by box.

w9.description:
W9 is where the payer's W-9 request to this payee stands: none, requested,
granted, declined or revoked.

forms.description: Forms are the drafts made or refreshed.

skipped.description:
Skipped says, per payee and form, why nothing was prepared — a form already
furnished is never re-prepared, only corrected.

businessName.description: BusinessName is line 2: the business or disregarded entity name.

certification.description: Certification is where the Part II signature stands.

consent.description:
Consent is the electronic-delivery consent. Only the org itself reads it: how
a payee takes delivery is not a payer's to know.

disclosure.description: Disclosure is the electronic-delivery disclosure the consent is given against.

exemptPayee.description: ExemptPayee is line 4's exempt payee code, 1–13.

expires.description:
Expires is when a certified W-8 stops being valid, unix seconds: the last
day of the third calendar year after the year it was signed. A W-9 does not
expire.

fatca.description: FATCA is line 4's FATCA exemption code, A–M.

foreignOwners.description:
ForeignOwners is line 3b: a flow-through entity with foreign partners,
owners or beneficiaries.

foreignTin.description:
ForeignTIN is a W-8's foreign tax identifying number, masked. The full
number is answered only with the full TIN read.

form.description: Form is w9, w8ben or w8bene.

name.description:
Name is line 1: the name on the income tax return, or of the foreign
individual or organization that is the beneficial owner.

phone.description: Phone is the number a 1099 this org files as PAYER prints for it.

tin.description:
TIN is Part I, masked to its last four digits. The full number is answered
only by GET /v1/tax/w9/{id}/tin, to a payer this org granted it to.

tinType.description: TINType is which Part I box: ssn (an SSN or ITIN) or ein.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when the profile last changed, unix seconds.

valid.description:
Valid is whether the form establishes what it certifies today — for a W-8,
certified for its current version and not expired; for a W-9, a TIN on file.

version.description: Version counts the W-9's revisions; a certification covers exactly one.

w8.description: W8 is what a W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E certifies beyond name and address.

code.description: Code is the rule's stable name, for a caller that branches on it.

account.description: Account is the account number the form prints.

backup.description: Backup is the backup withholding the payer applied.

corrected.description: Corrected is true for a statement that corrects an earlier one.

furnishedAt.description: FurnishedAt is when it was delivered, unix seconds.

id.description: ID is the form id the payer issued it under.

payer.description: Payer is the org that furnished it.

recipient.description: Recipient is this org, as the form names it, TIN truncated.

supersededBy.description: SupersededBy is the later statement that corrects this one.

supersedes.description: Supersedes is the earlier statement this corrects.

year.description: Year is the calendar year of the payments.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is the reportable payments in this box, summed exactly and then
rounded to cents.

box.description: Box is the form and box.

payments.description: Payments are the ids that sum into it.

reportable.description: Reportable is true when the total is at or above the threshold.

rule.description: Rule states the comparison and its source.

thresholdCents.description: ThresholdCents is the year's threshold for this box.

article.description: Article is the treaty article and paragraph claimed, e.g. "12(2)".

conditions.description:
Conditions is the explanation the form asks for: the conditions of the
article the beneficial owner meets.

country.description: Country is the treaty country the beneficial owner is resident in.

income.description:
Income is the type of income the claim covers: services, rents, royalties
or other.

lob.description:
LOB is W-8BEN-E line 14b: the treaty's limitation on benefits provision the
entity meets. Required on a W-8BEN-E treaty claim; a W-8BEN has no line 14b.

rateBps.description:
RateBps is the claimed withholding rate in basis points: 0 is exempt,
1000 is 10%.

box.description: Box is where it is reported, when it is.

rules.description:
Rules are every rule that applied, in the order applied — the last one is
the verdict's reason.

birth.description: Birth is W-8BEN line 8, the individual's date of birth, YYYY-MM-DD.

capacity.description:
Capacity is the capacity in which the signer signs for the beneficial owner
— "Director", "Authorized officer". Required on a W-8BEN-E; on a W-8BEN, empty
when the beneficial owner signs.

chapter3.description:
Chapter3 is W-8BEN-E line 4. A W-8BEN's beneficial owner is an individual
and states none.

chapter4.description: Chapter4 is W-8BEN-E line 5, the FATCA status.

country.description:
Country is line 2: the country of citizenship (W-8BEN) or of incorporation
or organization (W-8BEN-E), ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

giin.description: GIIN is W-8BEN-E line 9a, when the chapter 4 status carries one.

noForeignTin.description:
NoForeignTIN is W-8BEN line 6b / W-8BEN-E line 9b's alternative: the
jurisdiction of residence does not require or issue a foreign TIN.

treaty.description:
Treaty is the claim of treaty benefits (W-8BEN Part II lines 9-10, W-8BEN-E
Part III lines 14-15), when one is made.

category.description:
Category is what the payer states it pays this payee for. Only the payer
sees it.

decidedAt.description: DecidedAt is when the payee last granted, declined or revoked.

id.description: ID addresses the relationship on both sides.

match.description: Match is the IRS TIN Matching result the payer recorded, when it recorded one.

payee.description: Payee is the org whose W-9 it is.

payer.description: Payer is the org that asked.

profile.description:
Profile is the payee's W-9, TIN masked — present only for the payer, only
while the grant is live.

requestedAt.description: RequestedAt is when the payer asked, unix seconds.

role.description: Role is the caller's side of it: payer or payee.

status.description: Status is requested, granted, declined or revoked.

dueCents.description:
DueCents is what 24% of the reported boxes comes to — what should have been
withheld. Nothing on Hanzo's rails withholds, so box 4 reports zero, and the
payer is liable for the amount it did not withhold (IRC §3403).

rate.description: Rate is the backup withholding rate, in percent: 24.

reason.description:
Reason says why, and which rule — or, when nothing is required, what the payer
should still know.

required.description:
Required is true when the payer holds no TIN for the payee — the IRC
§3406(a)(1)(A) trigger these forms can know. An uncertified W-9 is not one for
these payments, and says so in Reason without requiring anything.

boxes.description:
Boxes are the corrected amounts, by box. Omitted, the boxes are derived
again from the payments and the payee's W-9 is read again — which is also how a
wrong name or TIN is corrected. Zero in every box withdraws the return.

id.description: ID is the furnished form to correct, from the path.

reason.description: Reason says what was wrong. Required; it goes on the record.

data.description: Data are the filings, oldest first, without their files.
Data are the forms, oldest first.

id.description: ID is the relationship, from the path.

result.description:
Result is what IRS TIN Matching answered for this payee's name and TIN:
matched or mismatched.

year.description: Year is the calendar year the payments were made in.

address.description:
Address is W-9 lines 5 and 6, or a W-8's line 3 permanent residence address
outside the United States (state and zip where the country uses them).
Required: a statement owed on paper is mailed there.

businessName.description: BusinessName is line 2, when it differs from line 1.

classification.description:
Classification is W-9 line 3a: individual, c_corp, s_corp, partnership,
trust_estate, llc_c, llc_s or llc_p. Required on a W-9; absent on a W-8.

electronicConsent.description:
ElectronicConsent gives (true) or withdraws (false) consent to receive 1099s
in the Hanzo inbox, against the disclosure every profile answers with.
Omitted, the stored consent stands.

exemptPayee.description: ExemptPayee is the exempt payee code, 1–13. Entities only.

fatca.description: FATCA is the FATCA exemption code, A–M. Entities only.

foreignOwners.description: ForeignOwners is line 3b; only a partnership, trust/estate or llc_p may set it.

foreignTin.description:
ForeignTIN is a W-8's foreign tax identifying number (W-8BEN line 6a,
W-8BEN-E line 9b), as the jurisdiction of residence issues it. Omitted
afterwards, the stored number is kept; the empty string with
w8.noForeignTin clears it.

form.description:
Form is w9 (a U.S. person), w8ben (a foreign individual) or w8bene (a
foreign entity). w9 when omitted.

name.description:
Name is line 1: the name on the income tax return, or the foreign
individual's or organization's name. Required.

phone.description: Phone is printed on the 1099s this org files as payer.

tin.description:
TIN is W-9 Part I, or a W-8's U.S. TIN (W-8BEN line 5, W-8BEN-E line 8),
digits with or without hyphens. Required on a W-9's first write; on a W-8,
only for a treaty claim with no foreign TIN. Omitted afterwards, the stored
number is kept, so an address change never re-sends it.

tinType.description:
TINType is ssn (an SSN or ITIN) or ein. An entity other than an individual
states an EIN.

w8.description:
W8 is the rest of a W-8: the country of citizenship or incorporation, the
chapter 3 and chapter 4 statuses of an entity, a date of birth, the treaty
claim, and the signer's capacity. Required on a W-8; absent on a W-9.

id.description: ID is the filing, from the path.

receiptId.description: ReceiptID is the Receipt ID IRIS returned for the submission.

status.description:
Status is submitted (IRIS returned a Receipt ID), accepted,
accepted_with_errors or rejected (IRIS's acknowledgment).

tcc.description:
TCC is the IRIS Transmitter Control Code the payer submitted under: five
uppercase letters and digits.

data.description: Data are the statements, oldest first.

foreignTin.description:
ForeignTIN is a W-8 payee's foreign tax identifying number as issued, which
Form 1042-S carries for a foreign recipient.

tin.description:
TIN is the payee's full U.S. taxpayer identification number, hyphenated as
the IRS writes it; empty when a W-8 carries none.

asPayee.description: AsPayee are the requests for the caller's own W-9.

asPayer.description: AsPayer are the W-9s the caller asked for.

category.description:
Category is what the caller pays it for: services, attorney, rents,
royalties, other or merchandise. Services when omitted.

payee.description:
Payee is the org id of the company asked. The caller must have paid it on
Hanzo's rails.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
